newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan PM vows to bring in speedy trial law.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan PM vows to bring in speedy trial law.

text.p: Pakistani Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif said on Tuesday he would soon bring in a new law to fight ethnic and Moslem sectarian violence and he threatened to ban Islamic schools aiding such strife.
He told reporters that the new law to be brought before parliament would provide for quick trials.

"There is no option other than speedy courts as people want speedy trial of the terrorists," he said after a meeting of the parliamentary group of his Pakistan Muslim League party and its allies before the start of new National Assembly (lower house) and Senate (upper house) sessions.
"Speedy trial and punishment of those involved in heinous crimes are in line with the aspirations of the nation," he said.

Rival militants groups of the majority Sunni and the minority Shi'ite sects of Islam blame each other for a spate of attacks in Sharif's home province of Punjab, which have killed at least 145 people this year, including 15 last Saturday.
Ethnic and political violence has erupted again in the port city of Karachi, taking more than 225 lives this year compared to about 500 last year and more than 2,000 in 1995.

"The terrorists should be hanged so that others could not dare do such activities," Sharif said. "It's pitiable that the terrorists are roaming scot-free, while the administration and police have been terrorised."
He said some of the institutions run by various religious groups were teaching their students to kill members of rival sects so they could go to heaven in the hereafter.
"There is no justififcation for these nurseries for terrorism to exist," he said. "Closing of these institutions is a must for the survival of the country."
Sharif said some schools run by the Sunni sect taught their students to call Shi'ite "Kafirs" (infidels) while some Shi'ite schools told their students to brand Sunnis as "Murtads" (apostates).
"These people will not go to heaven, rather they will become fuel for hell," he said.

Sunni-Shi'ite disputes over Islamic beliefs have often spilled into violence in Pakistan. Sunnis dominate Pakistan's population of more than 135 million, while Shi'ites are about 15 percent but are the majority in neighbouring Iran.
